impacted.role: the _reextract_item helper (line 174) re-extracts an rss row with extract_article only; _refetch_one (line 220) analyses a recovered row through orchestrator.analyze_and_store_item or rewrites title_only on a still-unreadable one

the RssFetcher's _add_hn_discussion method (line 312), the one place a story's discussion is fetched and appended; the live loop (line 135) derives the HN id from the feed entry's comments link and records comments_outcome on the item (line 171)
story_id (line 58) reads the id from a whole comments-link string through _COMMENTS_LINK_RE (line 36), which is anchored at both ends, so it does not find the link inside stored HTML content

constraints.text: The rss branch of _reextract_item calls extract_article(row['url'], ...) and nothing else, so a refetched HN story never gets its discussion.
The HN id comes from entry.get('comments') at fetch time and is not persisted; external_id is a hash (cerebro rows such as 9c825ff1c4901a4c).

On cerebro on 2026-10-10: 47 non-archived title-only items from https://news.ycombinator.com/rss; 39 have unreadable content and every one of those contains news.ycombinator.com/item?id=<id>; the other 8 are model:not_substantive with readable content, which get_unreadable_content does not select.
The orchestrator holds the RSS fetcher as self.rss_fetcher, which refetch already reaches through the orchestrator it is given.
Principle I: third-party HTTP (HN's Firebase API) is the only thing faked in tests, through recorded vcrpy cassettes; internal code runs for real.

issues.why: a refetch policy for sources that update after fetch (Reddit threads, edited posts); this work does not re-read readable items, so #51 stays open and unaffected

reuse.what: the RssFetcher's _add_hn_discussion method, called from refetch rather than copied
the HN item-link pattern, shared by an unanchored search for the id inside stored content
